newsitem.title: USA: Blue Shield of California to buy CareAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Blue Shield of California to buy CareAmerica.

text.p: Blue Shield of California, the fifth largest health care provider in the state, said Tuesday it agreed to buy CareAmerica Health Plans and CareAmerica Life Insurance Co. from UniHealth for $175 million.
The acquisition will expand Blue Shield's presence in southern California by 265,000 members, more than 45,000 of whom are Medicare members.

Blue Shield, which operates as a not-for-profit health care provider, said it agreed to buy the CareAmerica units to help it improve its services. The acquisition will also make Blue Shield a more dominant player in the health maintenance organisation market.

The combined company will have more than 1.8 million members, more than 710,000 of whom are enrolled in an HMO. Blue Shield offers a variety of health plans and prior to the merger had slightly more than a quarter of its members enrolled in an HMO.
Revenue in the combined company will exceed $2 billion.

Blue Shield said it has been aggressively working in the past two years to increase HMO and preferred provider organisation health plan membership. But it contends that as a not-for-profit health care provider it is able to offer superior services to its members, such as direct access to specialists.

CareAmerica companies and Blue Shield will continue to operate independently until the acquisition is complete. Blue Shield said it expects the acquisition to be completed by the end of the year, subject to regulatory approvals.
